title: Database Migration
body:
A versioned, incremental, checked-in script that changes a database's schema — add a column, create an index, backfill a value. A blueprint for renovating storage over time, applied in order, so every environment (a teammate's laptop, staging, production) can be brought to the same schema state by running the same sequence.

The reason they exist: a schema can't be redeployed by overwriting it the way application code can, because it holds live data. Migrations turn schema evolution into an ordered, reviewable history rather than a set of manual `ALTER TABLE` statements someone ran once and forgot. They run on the server or in CI, against the database, as a deploy step. In [[Ruby on Rails]] they're first-class and generated alongside [[ActiveRecord]] models.
